S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive behaviors that are developmentally inappropriate, present in multiple settings, and cause clinically significant functional impairment. In adults, it often presents as disorganization, difficulty sustaining focus, restlessness, and impulsive decision-making rather than overt childhood-type hyperactivity, and symptoms must have been present since childhood even if they were partially compensated for or overlooked. The course is typically chronic, with fluctuating impact depending on environmental demands, stress, and structure, and is frequently complicated by comorbid anxiety, mood symptoms, or substance use. It is distinguished from anxiety, mood, and personality disorders by the early onset, cross-situational cognitive/behavioral pattern, and relative stability of core attentional and inhibitory control deficits across time, even when compensatory strategies are in place.

patient.personality: Outgoing, competitive, and talkative, Steven prides himself on his street smarts and charm, enjoys friendly rivalry, and throws himself enthusiastically into sports, grilling, and tinkering with gadgets and cars.
patient.stressor: Roughly a year and a half ago, Steven’s courier company adopted new dispatch software and tighter performance metrics, shifting his job from relying mainly on intuition and local knowledge to following complex digital routing, scanning, and documentation procedures. While he had always managed his distractible tendencies with experience and hustle, the constant app notifications, strict time windows, and detailed electronic logs made it harder for him to stay mentally locked onto one task without drifting into conversation, sports talk, or thoughts about his side projects. Over time, small errors—missed special delivery instructions, incomplete scans, and occasional mis-sequenced stops—began to show up in his performance reports, threatening his hopes for a future dispatch manager role and leading to more friction with younger supervisors who saw him as careless rather than overwhelmed by the new cognitive demands. After several months of increasing frustration, along with feedback from his wife and bowling teammates that he seemed more scattered and forgetful whenever he talked about work, he agreed to see a psychiatrist when his primary care doctor suggested that long-standing attention issues might be surfacing more clearly now that his job had become more structured and mentally demanding.
patient.chief_complaint: “I just can’t seem to keep my mind on my route from start to finish anymore—I lose focus halfway through and then my deliveries get all out of order.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: With this new delivery app, I’ll skim the instructions, think I’ve got it, and then later find out I missed a note like ‘leave at side door only’ or typed the wrong apartment number because I was rushing and not really zoomed in on the tiny details.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: I can start my route focused, but halfway through a long stretch my mind just slides off the screen and I’m thinking about last night’s game or my car project, and I have to keep checking the app again because I don’t remember the last few stops it showed me.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: My supervisor will tell me, ‘Scan it, get a signature, take a picture, then mark it delivered,’ and I’ll scan it and drop the box, but I’ll drive off and realize I never did the photo or the final tap on the app, so it looks like I never finished the job.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: I’ll be standing at the back of the truck trying to sort packages, and a text buzzes or a guy walks by talking about the Bears, and next thing I know I’ve stopped sorting and I’m either answering the text or half listening to their conversation instead of finishing what I was doing.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: My wife gets on me because I’ll say I’ll pay the electric bill or call the mechanic on my lunch break, then I get caught up chatting with the guys or chasing a delivery time and completely forget until we get a late notice or she reminds me that night.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: Even when I’m just sitting in a meeting at work or watching TV with my wife, my leg is bouncing, my fingers are drumming on the table, or I’m flipping my keys in my hand without even realizing I’m doing it.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Any time I’m stuck in one spot for a while, like at those longer safety meetings or waiting in the doctor’s office, I feel this pent-up energy like I’ve got to get up and move around, and I’m shifting in my chair and looking for an excuse to step outside.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: On my days off I tell myself I’ll just sit and read or watch a movie quietly, but after a few minutes I’m talking over the show, checking my phone, or getting up to tinker with the grill because just sitting there still and quiet makes me antsy.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My family jokes that I can’t just relax, because even after a full day on the road I’ll come home and start rearranging the garage, firing up the grill, or messing with the car instead of just sitting down like a normal person.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: When I’m in line at the post office or waiting for my turn at the bowling alley, I get really impatient, keep checking the time, and catch myself wanting to jump ahead or push things along because just standing there waiting drives me nuts.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: My wife and my buddies at bowling tell me I cut people off a lot, because as soon as I get an idea or think I know where their story is going, I jump in and start talking over them without meaning to.
